vendors.name: Google
vendors.service: large language model API for the AI assistants and the control mapper
vendors.plain: Google supplies the AI model (Gemini 2.5 Flash) behind the assistants and the control mapper. Conversation text passes through its service while an answer is generated; no customer account data is sent.
data_access: support and sales conversation text in transit

contract.data_location: not region-pinned on the Gemini Developer API; regional processing would require the Vertex AI path
contract.note: Standard Gemini API paid-tier terms (the Nimbus relationship is simulated; the terms are real). Prompts and responses are processed under Google's Data Processing Addendum for Products Where Google is a Data Processor, which commits to notifying the customer of a data incident promptly and without undue delay. No fixed hour count is published, so the field is null. Under the paid tier Google does not use prompts or responses to improve its products.

vendors.concentration: single model vendor: every assistant and the control mapper call the same provider. The model name is pinned by environment variable, so a switch is a configuration change and a regression run, not a rewrite; there is no qualified second provider today (see R-05).

vendors.name: Vercel
vendors.service: hosting, serverless functions and analytics for the AI assistants and this trust center
vendors.plain: Vercel runs the web pages and the small server programs behind the assistants and this site. It sees requests as they pass through and holds the model key as an environment variable, but stores no conversation content.
data_access: support and sales conversation text in transit through serverless functions
visitor IP addresses and request metadata used for rate limiting and analytics
the model API key, held as a platform environment variable

contract.data_location: US by default; the serverless function region is a deployment setting
contract.note: Standard self-serve terms (the Nimbus relationship is simulated; the terms are real). The Vercel Data Processing Addendum commits to notifying the customer of a confirmed security incident without undue delay. No fixed hour count is published, so the field is null. Assurance is by the published SOC 2 Type 2 report and ISO 27001 certificate rather than a negotiated audit right.

vendors.concentration: single hosting provider: the assistants and this trust center both run on one provider, so one outage takes both down. The simulated Nimbus product itself runs on the primary cloud provider (V-07).

vendors.name: GitHub
vendors.service: source control and continuous integration for the AI assistants and this trust center
vendors.plain: GitHub stores the source code and runs the automated checks before every release. It holds code and test fixtures, not customer data, and the secrets are deliberately kept out of it.
data_access: source code, build configuration and test fixtures
no customer data; no secrets (the repository is secret-scanned on every build)

contract.note: Standard terms (the Nimbus relationship is simulated; the terms are real). The GitHub Data Protection Agreement commits to notifying the customer of a security incident promptly and without undue delay. No fixed hour count is published, so the field is null.

vendors.concentration: none noted: an outage delays deployments but does not take the live sites or the product down

vendors.name: Keystone Identity
vendors.service: workforce identity: single sign-on, multi-factor authentication and directory
vendors.plain: The service staff use to sign in to company systems with a second factor. It holds staff identities and login records, not customer data. Invented for the story; not a real company.
data_access: staff identities, group memberships and authentication logs
vendors.concentration: single identity provider: if it is down, staff cannot sign in to most systems; break-glass administrator accounts with hardware keys are held offline for that case

vendors.name: Ledgerline Payments
vendors.plain: The payment company that takes card payments for Nimbus subscriptions. Card numbers go straight to it and never touch Nimbus systems, which is what keeps Nimbus on the lightest card-security self-assessment. Invented for the story; not a real company.
data_access: cardholder data (held entirely by the processor, never by Nimbus)
customer billing contact details and invoice amounts
vendors.pci_dss: Attestation of Compliance on file (PCI DSS v4.0.1, Level 1 service provider); Nimbus completes SAQ A because the processor holds all card data
vendors.concentration: single payment processor: an outage pauses new sign-ups and renewals but does not affect the product; the exposure is revenue timing, not customer data

vendors.name: Harbor HRIS
vendors.service: human resources information system and payroll
vendors.plain: The system that holds employee records and runs payroll. It holds staff data, not customer data, and its contract is missing a clause that would oblige it to report a breach quickly. Invented for the story; not a real company.
data_access: employee personal, payroll and benefits records
vendors.concentration: none noted: a payroll outage is handled by the provider's paper fallback and does not affect customers

vendors.name: Northwind Cloud
vendors.service: primary cloud platform for the Nimbus product: compute, managed database, object storage and backups
vendors.plain: The cloud provider that runs the Nimbus product and stores customer data. Everything the product holds sits on this provider, encrypted at rest, with backups copied to an isolated account. Invented for the story; not a real company.
data_access: customer account data and customer content (encrypted at rest)

contract.data_location: US, with an EU region for EU customer workspaces

vendors.concentration: single primary cloud provider for the product: backups are copied to an isolated account at the same provider, so a provider-wide failure is the residual exposure accepted under R-06
